title: 2020 - Pulling Starters - Unknown Authors
universal_lens: Bayesian updating in dynamic sports environments integrates optimal stopping with behavioral biases, explaining why managers often delay reliever substitutions despite deteriorating performance. Bullpen quality and recency effects are modeled via season-long WHIP and pitch count lags, with fixed effects for team and opponent contexts.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian updating in baseball management maps to conformal inference via sequential hypothesis testing, where managers process noisy pitch data to update beliefs about starter fatigue. Bayesian inference on starter pull decisions uses WHIP and bullpen pitch counts as probabilistic priors, with fixed effects for team-seasons and opponents to constrain posterior distributions.
gse_mapping: Baseball starter substitution models map to Markov decision processes, representing state transitions between innings, runs allowed, and win probabilities, with optimal stopping governed by information arrival rates. Situational reasoning maps starter pull decisions to state transitions using recent event variables and bullpen condition, enabling dynamic policy updates through temporal convolution.

primitives.name: Omission Bias
primitives.verbatim_quote: The omission bias— the bias toward favoring errors of omission and not commission (in our context, pulling the starter) (Ritov and Baron, 1990; Bar-Eli, Azar, Ritov, Keidar-Levin, and Schein, 2007)—could lead starters to be generally left in games too long.

primitives.breakdown_regime: When the cost of reliever usage is fixed and visible, the bias amplifies, causing delays until damage is irreversible.

layer2.mapping: Omission bias introduces a threshold effect in GSI's Bayesian updating framework, where the posterior odds ratio must exceed a higher hurdle before a pull decision is made compared to the economically efficient cutoff.
layer2.telemetry: Analysis of bullpen cost allocation patterns reveals that managers are more likely to leave starters in when relief costs are explicitly stated.

primitives.name: Optimal Stopping
primitives.verbatim_quote: Managers decide when to "pull" the starter (replace him with a reliever) based on evidence that the starter is tiring and other new information used to update beliefs throughout the game.

primitives.breakdown_regime: When the state process is non-Markovian due to hidden fatigue, the optimal policy becomes a threshold rule based on the posterior distribution.

layer2.mapping: The optimal stopping problem translates into a GSE state-transition model where the value function represents the marginal gain in win probability from pulling versus staying, aligning with real-time telemetry of pitch efficiency metrics.
